name: Yext
oneLiner: Publicly traded (NYSE: YEXT) digital presence platform for multi-location brands: listings, local pages, reviews and AI search visibility managed from one knowledge base.
bestFor: Multi-location and franchise restaurant brands whose main need is accurate listings and local search visibility across many locations, with review management alongside.

updates.text: Acquired Places Scout, a local search intelligence provider, to add competitive benchmarking.
Launched Yext Scout, an AI search and competitive intelligence agent that tracks brand visibility and sentiment across Google, Bing and AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity.
Popmenu expanded its partnership with Yext so restaurants can sync menus and listings and respond to reviews across 70+ platforms.

features: Central knowledge base (Knowledge Graph) that holds each location's hours, menus and details
Listings sync to Google, Apple Maps, Bing, Facebook and other directories and apps
Review monitoring for Google, Facebook, Yelp and 80+ industry sites in one dashboard, with smart filters and alerts
AI-drafted review replies that you approve, or replies that post automatically under rules you set
Review requests sent by email, text or QR code, with a balancing algorithm that routes them to the sites that most affect search visibility
Scout: visibility and sentiment tracking in traditional and AI search, with competitor benchmarks
Location landing pages (Yext Pages) for local SEO
Role-based access, audit trails and approval workflows for large teams and franchise networks

pricing.text: Custom pricing; Yext publishes no price list. Price depends on location count and the solution chosen, billing is typically annual, multi-year terms get a better rate than one-year terms, and there is no free tier or standard free trial (evaluation is through a demo). Smaller businesses are pointed to reseller partners.

notes: Dropped from the current review: the weekly prices ($4/$9/$10/$19 per week), which do not match any current source; '200+ direct integration partners' (not re-confirmed; SocialPilot says 80+ review platforms, Popmenu release says 70+). Corporate: CEO Michael Walrath's August 2025 $9/share take-private proposal was withdrawn on 2026-02-02 (financing not obtained) and replaced by a $150M Dutch-auction tender (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260202956818/en); Yext stays public. Hearsay Systems acquired August 2024. Arby's and Taco Bell stories are older vendor case studies. 2026-11: yext.com/pricing returns 404; the Yext FAQ (knowledge center) confirms custom pricing, annual billing, no free trial and reseller route for small businesses. '80+ industry sites' and the review features come from yext.com/platform/reviews. G2 rating seen only in search snippets of g2.com (4.4; review count varies between 1,008 and 1,126 across G2 pages), so reviews cite the score only.
pros: One knowledge base feeds listings, local pages and reviews, so a change to hours or menus is made once
Review monitoring across Google, Facebook, Yelp and 80+ industry sites, with AI-drafted replies you approve
Scout tracks visibility and sentiment in Google, Bing and AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, against competitors
Role-based access, audit trails and approval workflows built for franchise networks
Restaurant customers include Taco Bell, Arby's, Bojangles and Marston's

cons.text: No published prices: pricing is custom, set by location count and solution, and typically billed annually
No free tier and no standard free trial; you evaluate it through a demo
A one-year term costs more than a multi-year term
Smaller businesses are directed to reseller partners instead of buying from Yext directly
Listings and local search come first, with reviews alongside, so brands that mainly want post-visit guest surveys or support may need another tool

plans.billing: custom quote by location count and solution, typically billed annually
